The diagram follows `place_order` in `src/app.py`:
- It checks stock for every item first and rejects the order if any item is short.
- It then calls `charge`, which rejects the order if payment fails.
- If payment succeeds, it decrements stock, appends the order to `data/orders.json` and returns it as "placed".

The README says customers order through `POST /orders` and get an emailed receipt. The code has neither: `place_order` is a plain function and nothing sends email. I noted this in the doc rather than drawing flows that don't exist.

# shopfront

A tiny order service used as the fixture for Junior-dev's headless runs. Customers place
orders through `POST /orders`; the service checks stock, charges the card through the
payment provider, and records the order. Orders are kept in `data/orders.json`.

Run it with `python -m src.app`. It needs no database. You will recieve an email receipt
when an order is placed.

# Checkout flow

How `place_order(customer, items, card_token)` in `src/app.py` works.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor C as Customer
    participant A as app.place_order
    participant S as STOCK (in memory)
    participant P as payments.charge
    participant F as data/orders.json

    C->>A: place_order(customer, items, card_token)
    loop each item
        A->>S: STOCK.get(name, 0) >= qty?
    end
    alt any item short
        A-->>C: rejected, "out of stock: <name>"
    else all in stock
        Note over A: total = sum(PRICES[name] * qty), in cents
        A->>P: charge(card_token, total)
        Note over P: Never raises. Empty token gives ok=False
        alt payment not ok
            P-->>A: {ok: false}
            A-->>C: rejected, "payment failed"
        else payment ok
            P-->>A: {ok: true, id: "pay_..."}
            A->>S: decrement stock per item
            A->>F: read existing orders (or [])
            Note over A: id = len(orders) + 1
            A->>F: append order and write file
            A-->>C: placed, order
        end
    end
```

## Notes

- Stock is checked before payment, but only decremented after payment succeeds.
- Stock lives in memory only, so it resets on restart. Orders persist in the JSON file.
- The README mentions `POST /orders` and an emailed receipt. Neither exists in the code. `place_order` is a plain function, and nothing sends email.
- Unknown item names fail the stock check (`STOCK.get(name, 0)`). Stock is checked first, so `PRICES[name]` is never reached for them.
